preferred_position: Mutual confidentiality covering all non-public information, with the standard exclusions, surviving at least 3 years after the agreement ends (trade secrets for as long as they remain secret).
fallback_position: 2 years' survival for general information if trade secrets stay protected indefinitely.
rationale: Our business and product information must stay protected after the relationship ends.

preferred_position: The consultant discloses conflicts of interest and does not advise our competitors on the same matter during the engagement.
fallback_position: Disclosure of conflicts only.
rationale: Advice must be independent of competing interests.

preferred_position: The consultant is an independent contractor: no employment relationship, the consultant pays its own taxes and benefits, and uses its own tools.
rationale: Misclassification creates employment and tax liability for us.

preferred_position: Everything the consultant creates for us is assigned to us on creation, with moral rights waived where the law allows.
fallback_position: Assignment on payment of the related invoice.
rationale: Advice and material we pay for must be ours to use.

preferred_position: Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid under the agreement. Indirect and consequential losses are excluded. The cap does not apply to breach of confidentiality, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
fallback_position: Up to 2x the fees.
rationale: The cap decides the most we can lose on this contract; carve-outs keep the risks a cap must not cover.

preferred_position: Neither party solicits the other's staff for 12 months after the engagement.
fallback_position: 6 months.
rationale: Protects our team.

preferred_position: Payment within 30 days of receipt of a valid, undisputed invoice. Disputed amounts may be withheld in good faith. No advance payment above 20% of the fees.
fallback_position: 45 days; expenses only if pre-approved in writing.
rationale: Protects cash flow and keeps leverage until the work is delivered.

preferred_position: We may terminate for convenience on 15 days' notice, paying for work properly done. Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days.
fallback_position: Termination for convenience on 60 days' notice.
rationale: We must be able to exit a relationship that no longer works without waiting for a breach.

preferred_position: Receiving Party must provide prompt written notice to Disclosing Party as soon as legally permissible (and in any event before disclosure) upon receipt of any legal process, subpoena, court order, or regulatory demand requiring disclosure of Confidential Information. Receiving Party must: (a) cooperate with Disclosing Party's efforts to seek a protective order or other relief; (b) disclose only the minimum amount legally required; and (c) use reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment for any disclosed information.
fallback_position: If notice before disclosure is legally prohibited (e.g., grand jury subpoena with gag order), accept notice as soon as legally permissible after disclosure, provided cooperation and minimum-disclosure obligations remain. Accept removal of the cooperation obligation only if counterparty is a regulated financial institution subject to regulatory examination.
prohibited_language: Any language that permits disclosure without any prior notice obligation. Any clause that deems legal compulsion a complete waiver of all confidentiality obligations beyond the specific compelled disclosure.
required_language: The Receiving Party shall: (a) provide prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party prior to any such disclosure to the extent permitted by law; (b) cooperate fully with the Disclosing Party in seeking a protective order, confidential treatment, or other appropriate relief; and (c) disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that is legally required to be disclosed.
rationale: Advance notice gives us the opportunity to seek injunctive relief or a protective order before sensitive information is disclosed in legal proceedings. The minimum-disclosure requirement limits collateral damage.

preferred_position: Broad definition capturing all non-public information disclosed in any form (written, oral, electronic, visual), whether or not marked 'Confidential,' including technical data, trade secrets, business plans, financial data, customer lists, and AI/ML training data, datasets, model weights, and outputs derived from our information.
fallback_position: Accept a narrower definition limited to information marked 'Confidential' at time of disclosure, provided oral disclosures are confirmed in writing within 10 business days, and AI/ML data and training prohibitions are preserved as a standalone clause.
prohibited_language: Any language that excludes AI-generated outputs, model training data, or derivative works from the definition of Confidential Information. Any blanket exclusion of orally disclosed information without a written confirmation mechanism.
required_language: Confidential Information expressly includes: (a) all data, datasets, and information used to train, fine-tune, or evaluate any artificial intelligence or machine learning model; (b) outputs, embeddings, or derivative works generated using Disclosing Party's Confidential Information; and (c) the fact that discussions between the parties are occurring.
rationale: An overly narrow definition creates gaps that counterparties can exploit to use sensitive data — especially AI/ML data — without restriction. Broad coverage is our first line of defense. AI-data prohibitions are non-negotiable given the irreversible nature of model training.

preferred_position: Standard four-part exclusions only: (1) publicly available information (not due to breach); (2) independently developed without use of Confidential Information; (3) rightfully received from a third party without restriction; (4) already known to Receiving Party prior to disclosure (with documentary evidence required).
fallback_position: Accept the standard four exclusions but insist that the burden of proving any exclusion applies rests on the Receiving Party, and that exclusions must be established by clear and convincing written evidence.
prohibited_language: Any exclusion for information that 'becomes generally known through no fault of the Receiving Party' without a direct causal link to a breach. Any exclusion for information developed by employees who 'had no access' to Confidential Information (too difficult to verify and enforce).
required_language: The Receiving Party bears the burden of proving by clear and convincing written evidence that any exclusion applies. No combination or aggregation of non-confidential elements shall be deemed non-confidential if the combination itself constitutes Confidential Information.
rationale: Overly broad exclusions are a common counterparty tactic to carve out large swaths of information. The mosaic/aggregation carve-out is critical for protecting compiled datasets and AI training corpora.

preferred_position: Governing law and courts: any one of India, England and Wales, Singapore, New York or Delaware is acceptable, chosen per transaction. Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the chosen jurisdiction, waives any objection to personal jurisdiction or venue (including inconvenient forum), and, to the extent permitted by the governing law, waives trial by jury.
fallback_position: Accept mutual/non-exclusive jurisdiction if the counterparty is in a different jurisdiction, provided the governing law remains one of India, England and Wales, Singapore, New York or Delaware. Accept the counterparty's choice of any of those five. Escalate to Legal if the counterparty insists on any governing law or jurisdiction outside the five.
prohibited_language: Any governing law other than India, England and Wales, Singapore, New York or Delaware, unless Legal has approved it. Any arbitration clause that would delay or prevent emergency injunctive relief. Any clause requiring disputes to be resolved exclusively in a jurisdiction outside those five without our consent.
required_language: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the chosen jurisdiction (India, England and Wales, Singapore, New York or Delaware), without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction for resolution of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
rationale: The five jurisdictions (India, England and Wales, Singapore, New York, Delaware) are accepted for NDAs, so a choice of any of them needs no escalation. Exclusive jurisdiction prevents counterparties from forum-shopping. Jury trial waiver (where enforceable) reduces litigation risk and cost.

preferred_position: Confidential Information may be used solely for the expressly defined Purpose stated in the Agreement. Standard of care: the higher of (a) reasonable care or (b) the same degree of care used to protect the Receiving Party's own confidential information of like sensitivity, but in no event less than a high degree of care. Disclosure limited to employees/contractors with a strict need-to-know who are bound by written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Agreement.
fallback_position: Accept 'reasonable care' as the standard if counterparty resists 'high degree of care,' provided the need-to-know restriction and written obligation requirement for sub-disclosees are preserved. Accept Purpose limited to evaluation of a potential business relationship if the Purpose is currently undefined.
prohibited_language: Any language permitting use of Confidential Information for AI/ML model training, benchmarking, or product development outside the defined Purpose. Any standard of care below 'reasonable care.' Any provision allowing disclosure to affiliates or subsidiaries without written confidentiality obligations.
required_language: The Receiving Party shall not use Confidential Information to train, fine-tune, test, or otherwise develop any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, algorithm, or system. Disclosure to third-party service providers requires prior written consent of the Disclosing Party.
rationale: Limiting use to the defined Purpose and imposing a high standard of care are our primary operational controls. The AI/ML use prohibition is critical and non-negotiable — once data is used in model training it cannot be 'returned' or 'destroyed' in any meaningful sense.

preferred_position: Mutual acknowledgment that breach or threatened breach will cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are an inadequate remedy, entitling the non-breaching party to seek injunctive or other equitable relief without the requirement to post a bond or other security, and without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available at law or in equity.
fallback_position: Accept a requirement to post a nominal bond (not to exceed $[10,000]) if counterparty insists, provided the mutual availability of injunctive relief and the 'inadequate remedy' acknowledgment are preserved. Do not accept a unilateral injunctive relief clause that benefits only the counterparty.
prohibited_language: Any clause limiting remedies to monetary damages only. Any waiver of the right to seek injunctive or equitable relief. Any unilateral injunctive relief provision that does not apply equally to both parties. Any limitation of liability clause that caps damages in a way that would effectively preclude meaningful recovery for breach of confidentiality.
required_language: Each party acknowledges that a breach or threatened breach of this Agreement would cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy, and that the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief without the requirement to post bond or other security.
rationale: Injunctive relief is our most powerful enforcement tool for NDA breaches — it allows us to stop ongoing harm immediately. Mutual availability ensures we are not disadvantaged. Waiving the bond requirement removes a practical barrier to emergency relief.

preferred_position: Upon expiration, termination, or written request by Disclosing Party, Receiving Party must promptly (within 10 business days) return all tangible Confidential Information and permanently delete/destroy all electronic copies, including copies in backup systems, with written certification of destruction signed by an authorized officer. No retention of copies permitted except as required by applicable law or regulation (with notice to Disclosing Party).
fallback_position: Accept a 30-day return/destruction window if counterparty resists 10 days. Accept retention of copies in automated backup systems that are not accessible in the ordinary course of business, provided such copies are overwritten in the normal backup cycle and remain subject to confidentiality obligations. Require written certification in all cases.
prohibited_language: Any language permitting indefinite retention of Confidential Information after termination. Any clause that deems destruction of electronic copies 'commercially impracticable' without a defined alternative obligation. Any provision allowing retention for 'internal business purposes' without limitation.
required_language: Within ten (10) business days of expiration, termination, or written request, the Receiving Party shall return or permanently destroy all Confidential Information (including all copies, extracts, and derivatives) and provide written certification of such return or destruction signed by an authorized representative.
rationale: Return/destruction obligations limit our exposure after the relationship ends. Written certification creates an evidentiary record. The backup-system carve-out is a practical concession but must be time-limited and subject to ongoing confidentiality obligations.

preferred_position: Agreement term of 3 years with confidentiality obligations surviving for 5 years post-expiration for general Confidential Information, and indefinitely (or for the life of the trade secret) for information constituting trade secrets under applicable law.
fallback_position: Accept a 2-year agreement term with 3-year post-expiration confidentiality survival for general information, provided trade secrets are carved out with indefinite or statutory protection. Do not accept any sunset on trade secret obligations.
prohibited_language: Any fixed expiration of confidentiality obligations for trade secrets. Any clause stating obligations expire upon termination of the agreement without a survival carve-out. Any 'sunset' provision shorter than 2 years for general Confidential Information.
required_language: Notwithstanding the foregoing, confidentiality obligations with respect to information constituting a trade secret under applicable law shall survive indefinitely or for so long as such information retains its status as a trade secret, whichever is longer.
rationale: A 2-year hard stop is our internal default floor. Trade secret protection must be indefinite — a fixed term on trade secrets is legally inconsistent with trade secret law in most jurisdictions and creates unnecessary exposure.

preferred_position: No exclusivity and no most-favoured-customer pricing.
rationale: Exclusivity or MFN pricing restricts the rest of our business.

preferred_position: Indian law with courts or arbitration seated in India.
fallback_position: English law with arbitration in Singapore for foreign customers.
rationale: Enforcement abroad is slow and costly.

preferred_position: We indemnify only for third-party IP infringement by our products, with the usual exclusions (customer modifications, combinations, misuse).
fallback_position: Add indemnity for our breach of law.
rationale: Broad indemnities make us insurer of the customer's business.

preferred_position: We keep all IP in our products and know-how; the customer gets a licence to use what it buys.
rationale: Assigning our IP to one customer stops us selling it to others.

preferred_position: Our total liability is capped at the fees paid by the customer in the 12 months before the claim, with indirect and consequential losses excluded.
fallback_position: Up to 2x annual fees; uncapped only for our breach of confidentiality.
rationale: Uncapped exposure to a customer can exceed the whole value of the deal.

preferred_position: Payment within 30–45 days of invoice, interest on late payment, and the right to suspend after 30 days overdue.
fallback_position: 60 days for strategic customers with Finance approval.
rationale: Our cash flow must not depend on the customer's own customers paying.

preferred_position: Service credits are the sole remedy for missed service levels and capped at 10% of monthly fees.
fallback_position: 15% cap.
rationale: Uncapped penalties can wipe out the margin on the deal.

preferred_position: We warrant the products work materially as documented for 90 days; all other warranties are disclaimed.
fallback_position: 12-month warranty with repair, replace or refund as the only remedy.
rationale: Open-ended warranties are unpriced risk.

preferred_position: We may audit, or receive independent audit reports, to verify compliance.
fallback_position: Annual independent report (ISO 27001 / SOC 2) instead of on-site audits.
rationale: Lets us demonstrate our own compliance.

preferred_position: Personal data breaches are notified to us without undue delay and within 48 hours, with the details we need to notify regulators and individuals.
fallback_position: Within 72 hours.
rationale: We have our own statutory notice deadlines.

preferred_position: The processor helps us answer data subject requests promptly.
rationale: We must meet statutory response times.

preferred_position: No transfer outside India (or the EEA for EU data) without Standard Contractual Clauses or another lawful safeguard.
rationale: Unlawful transfers carry regulatory penalties.

preferred_position: The processor processes personal data only on our documented instructions and for the stated purpose.
rationale: Required by the DPDP Act and GDPR; processing beyond instructions is a breach.

preferred_position: At the end of the services, personal data is returned or deleted at our choice, and deletion is certified.
rationale: Data must not outlive its purpose.

preferred_position: Appropriate technical and organisational measures, described in an annex, including encryption and access control.
rationale: Security obligations must be concrete enough to check.

preferred_position: Sub-processors only with our prior written authorisation, bound by the same obligations, with the processor fully liable for them.
fallback_position: General authorisation with 30 days' notice and a right to object.
rationale: We stay responsible for everyone who touches the data.

preferred_position: Mutual confidentiality covering all non-public information, with the standard exclusions, surviving at least 3 years after the agreement ends (trade secrets for as long as they remain secret).
fallback_position: 2 years' survival for general information if trade secrets stay protected indefinitely.
rationale: Our business and product information must stay protected after the relationship ends.

preferred_position: Where personal data is processed: comply with the DPDP Act 2023 (and GDPR where it applies), a DPA on our template, breach notice within 72 hours, and no transfer outside India without safeguards.
fallback_position: The counterparty's DPA if it meets the same standards; Privacy review required.
rationale: Personal data breaches carry statutory penalties and notice deadlines.

preferred_position: The provider defends and indemnifies us against third-party claims arising from its breach, negligence, wilful misconduct or infringement of third-party IP.
fallback_position: Indemnity limited to IP infringement and breach of law, with defence controlled by the indemnifying party.
rationale: Third-party claims caused by the other side must not land on us.

preferred_position: The provider holds commercial general liability and professional indemnity insurance appropriate to the services for the term and 1 year after.
fallback_position: Certificates on request instead of named-insured status.
rationale: Insurance stands behind the provider's indemnities.

preferred_position: Deliverables created for us belong to us on payment. The provider keeps its pre-existing IP and grants us a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it within the deliverables.
fallback_position: Provider owns generic tools; we own everything specific to our business and data.
rationale: We pay for the work, so we must be able to use and change it without the provider.

preferred_position: Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim. Indirect and consequential losses are excluded. The cap does not apply to breach of confidentiality, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
fallback_position: Up to 2x the annual fees; anything higher needs Legal Counsel approval.
rationale: The cap decides the most we can lose on this contract; carve-outs keep the risks a cap must not cover.

preferred_position: Payment within 45 days of receipt of a valid, undisputed invoice. Disputed amounts may be withheld in good faith. No advance payment above 20% of the fees.
fallback_position: 60 days if the provider accepts milestone payments tied to acceptance.
rationale: Protects cash flow and keeps leverage until the work is delivered.

preferred_position: Services meet agreed service levels with service credits for misses and a right to terminate for repeated failure.
fallback_position: Service credits only, capped at 10% of monthly fees.
rationale: Without measurable service levels there is no remedy short of termination.

preferred_position: We may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice, paying for work properly done. Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days.
fallback_position: Termination for convenience on 60 days' notice.
rationale: We must be able to exit a relationship that no longer works without waiting for a breach.

preferred_position: Our data is hosted in India (or the EU). Any transfer outside needs Standard Contractual Clauses or an equivalent safeguard and Privacy approval.
rationale: Cross-border transfers carry regulatory conditions.

preferred_position: The provider holds ISO 27001 or SOC 2 Type II, encrypts our data in transit and at rest, and notifies us of a security incident within 72 hours.
fallback_position: Equivalent controls evidenced by a security questionnaire reviewed by Compliance.
rationale: Our data in someone else's system is only as safe as their controls.

preferred_position: On termination we can export all our data in a standard format for 30 days, after which the provider deletes it and certifies deletion.
fallback_position: Export on request for 15 days.
rationale: We must never be locked in by our own data.

preferred_position: Each party's total liability is capped at 12 months' fees, with a higher cap (at least 3x fees) for data breaches. Indirect and consequential losses are excluded. The cap does not apply to breach of confidentiality, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
fallback_position: A single cap of 2x annual fees covering data breaches.
rationale: The cap decides the most we can lose on this contract; carve-outs keep the risks a cap must not cover.

preferred_position: Payment within 45 days of receipt of a valid, undisputed invoice. Disputed amounts may be withheld in good faith. No advance payment above 20% of the fees.
fallback_position: Annual in advance only for subscriptions under INR 10 lakh.
rationale: Protects cash flow and keeps leverage until the work is delivered.

preferred_position: Price increases on renewal are capped at 5% a year and notified at least 90 days in advance.
fallback_position: Capped at 8% or CPI, whichever is lower.
rationale: Avoids unbudgeted jumps once we depend on the system.

preferred_position: Renewal only with at least 60 days' notice to cancel, and a reminder from the provider before it renews.
fallback_position: 30 days' notice to cancel.
rationale: Silent auto-renewal commits budget we have not approved.

preferred_position: At least 99.5% monthly availability, with service credits for misses and a right to terminate after repeated failure.
fallback_position: 99% availability with service credits.
rationale: Downtime of a system we depend on stops our work.

preferred_position: We accept deliverables in writing after testing against agreed acceptance criteria within 10 working days.
fallback_position: Deemed acceptance only after 15 working days and a reminder.
rationale: Deemed acceptance lets the provider invoice for work we have not checked.

preferred_position: Changes to scope, fees or dates only through a written change order signed by both parties.
rationale: Stops scope creep through emails and calls.

preferred_position: Fixed fee or time-and-materials with a not-to-exceed cap; rates as in the master agreement.
fallback_position: Rates up to 5% above the master rate card with Finance approval.
rationale: Uncapped time-and-materials has no budget ceiling.

preferred_position: Named key personnel are not replaced without our consent.
rationale: We engaged these people for this work.

preferred_position: Payments are tied to accepted milestones, not to dates.
rationale: We pay for delivered value, not the passage of time.

preferred_position: The master agreement prevails over the SoW, except for scope and fees stated in the SoW.
rationale: A SoW must not quietly override the negotiated master terms (liability, IP, data).

preferred_position: Every deliverable is named with a due date and an owner; anything not listed is out of scope.
rationale: Vague scope is the most common cause of disputes and overruns.

preferred_position: We may audit the vendor's records relating to the agreement on reasonable notice.
fallback_position: Audit by an independent auditor once a year.
rationale: Lets us verify charges and compliance.

preferred_position: The vendor complies with anti-bribery, sanctions, labour and environmental law and our supplier code of conduct, and we may terminate for breach.
rationale: A supplier's breach of law becomes our reputational and legal problem.

preferred_position: Where personal data is processed: comply with the DPDP Act 2023 (and GDPR where it applies), a DPA on our template, breach notice within 72 hours, and no transfer outside India without safeguards.
fallback_position: The counterparty's DPA if it meets the same standards; Privacy review required.
rationale: Personal data breaches carry statutory penalties and notice deadlines.

preferred_position: The vendor defends and indemnifies us against third-party claims arising from defective goods, its breach of law, negligence or infringement of third-party IP.
fallback_position: Indemnity limited to IP infringement and breach of law, with defence controlled by the indemnifying party.
rationale: Third-party claims caused by the other side must not land on us.

preferred_position: Each party's total liability is capped at 12 months' fees for the vendor, with no cap on its indemnities. Indirect and consequential losses are excluded. The cap does not apply to breach of confidentiality, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud.
fallback_position: Vendor cap at 1x annual fees if indemnities stay uncapped.
rationale: The cap decides the most we can lose on this contract; carve-outs keep the risks a cap must not cover.

preferred_position: Payment within 45 days of receipt of a valid, undisputed invoice. Disputed amounts may be withheld in good faith. No advance payment above 20% of the fees.
fallback_position: 60 days for strategic suppliers.
rationale: Protects cash flow and keeps leverage until the work is delivered.

preferred_position: The vendor may not subcontract or assign without our written consent and stays responsible for its subcontractors.
rationale: We chose this vendor; others must not do the work without our say.

preferred_position: The vendor warrants that goods and services conform to the specification, are free from defects for at least 12 months, and are supplied with reasonable skill and care.
fallback_position: 6-month warranty with repair or replacement at the vendor's cost.
rationale: Warranties give us a remedy when what we buy fails.
